findings.problem: fs::read_to_string is a file I/O call hidden inside load_sessions which returns a plain Vec<Record>, making the function appear pure to callers. I/O must be in the shell layer.
findings.failure_mode: A caller expecting deterministic, cacheable behavior will be surprised by disk reads; testability is broken and the function cannot be unit-tested without fixture files.
findings.fix: Split load_sessions into a pure parse_lines(input: &[&str]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> and a shell function that reads the file and delegates to the pure parser.

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any file-read error (missing file, permission denied, I/O error).
findings.failure_mode: Unstructured panic instead of typed error; process aborts on recoverable conditions.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and map the IO error with .map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e)) instead of unwrap().

findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV data aborts the entire batch instead of returning a typed parse error.
findings.fix: Use .map_err(|e| ParseError::Invalid(value)) and return Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> from the parser.

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] are unchecked indexing into a Vec with no length validation.
findings.failure_mode: Short or empty lines cause panic via IndexOutofBounds instead of a typed error.
findings.fix: Validate parts.len() == 2 with .ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) or use get(0).get(1) with ok_or, and return typed error.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 performs a lossy cast from u32 to u16. Values > 65535 silently truncate.
findings.failure_mode: Domain invariants are violated: Record.value can hold truncated/wrong data instead of an error, corrupting downstream logic.
findings.fix: Parse directly into u16: .parse::<u16>().map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid), or use u32::try_from(value).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) after parsing as u32.

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is console I/O inside the parsing/record-construction logic.
findings.failure_mode: Side effects in pure logic make output non-deterministic, break test isolation, and leak the shell layer into the data layer.
findings.fix: Remove println! entirely. If logging is needed, pass a callback or return a log event from the shell, not the parser.

findings.problem: File I/O (line 9), parsing (lines 11-15), console logging (line 16), and domain construction (lines 17-20) are all fused in a single function. Data/Calculations/Actions architecture is violated.
findings.failure_mode: Cannot reason about, test, or verify the pure logic independently of I/O side effects; violates the mandatory architecture.
findings.fix: Extract three layers: (1) shell: file I/O and logging, (2) parser: pure fn parse_line(&str) -> Result<Record, ParseError>, (3) data: the Record struct itself.

findings.problem: The function returns Vec<Record> with no error type. All failures (IO, parse, index, overflow) collapse into panics.
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot distinguish or handle different failure modes; no recovery path exists.
findings.fix: Define a ParseError enum with variants like { Io(std::io::Error), Invalid, Empty, TooFew, TooMany, Overflow } and return Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>.

findings.problem: Raw primitives cross the parse boundary: path is &str and line content is unvalidated string data. No fallible smart constructor exists to enforce domain invariants, so callers can construct invalid Record values directly through the parser.
findings.failure_mode: The function accepts hostile input without any boundary validation, allowing malformed data to reach the domain.
findings.fix: Introduce a parse_boundary function or smart constructor that validates input format, length, and value ranges with typed errors before creating Record instances.

findings.problem: No max line count cap, no try_reserve, and no bounded allocation. The Vec grows unbounded based on file size.
findings.failure_mode: Large input files can exhaust memory; no allocation budget or graceful allocation-failure handling exists.
findings.fix: Validate max_lines before iterating, then use Vec::new() followed by out.try_reserve(max_lines).map_err(|_| ParseError::Allocation) after cap validation.

findings.problem: Uses line.split(',').map(...).collect() which allocates the full split Vec and allocates trimmed Strings, instead of split_once which parses only the needed fields.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary intermediate allocation and String copies on every line; wasteful for the two-field CSV grammar.
findings.fix: Use let (_name, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid)?; to extract fields without collecting split results.

findings.problem: Record.name is a raw String with no validation invariants. If the name has domain rules (non-empty, length, characters), they are unenforced.
findings.failure_mode: Illegal name values (empty, whitespace-only, invalid characters) can exist in Record, making them unrepresentable states.
findings.fix: Use a Name newtype with a smart constructor that validates and returns Result<Name, ParseError>, or an enum with validated variants.

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists. The function performs file I/O, string allocation per line, and Vec growth with no measurement of performance characteristics.
findings.failure_mode: Performance claims cannot be verified; hot-path allocation patterns are unknown and unoptimized.
findings.fix: Add criterion or similar benchmark comparing this implementation against a bounded, try_reserve'd version with profiling evidence.

findings.problem: No test targets, no benches, and no CI configuration exist. The hardening checklist requires commands claimed to have run to actually have run and passed.
findings.failure_mode: No evidence that the code compiles, passes tests, or satisfies lint gates.
findings.fix: Add integration tests and at minimum verify: cargo check, cargo clippy with strict flags, and cargo test.

no command evidence: cargo fmt, cargo clippy, cargo test were not run

no stress test for large input files, empty files, malformed lines, or boundary values
